newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNITA officials in Angolan capital to join new govt.
newsitem.headline: UNITA officials in Angolan capital to join new govt.

text.p: Senior members of the former rebel UNITA movement arrived in the Angolan capital on Monday ahead of taking up positions in a government of national unity later this week.
U.N. officials said 29 UNITA deputies and two vice-ministers arrived with relatives on a U.N. flight from Bailundo, in Angola's central highlands.
The Hercules plane then returned to fetch another group of UNITA members expected to arrive in Luanda later on Monday evening.
The arrival of the UNITA officials is a key step for the establishment of a unity government which will include members of UNITA and the ruling MPLA, scheduled to be inaugurated on March 20.

The inauguration was originally planned for January 25 but postponed several times, mainly because of problems in finding an acceptable role for UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi, who controls much of Angola, including diamond-rich areas.
UNITA and the government signed a peace accord in 1994 which has brought Angola the longest period of relative peace since two decades of civil war erupted on independence from Portugal in 1975.

The U.N. has around 7,000 troops, military observers and civilian police from more than 30 countries in Angola, helping to implement the accord, which provides for demobilisation of thousands of former rebels and government fighters and the formation of a united army.
The mandate of the U.N. peacekeeping mission ends on March 31, and the Security Council has been keeping a close eye on the process, blaming UNITA for delays.
Even after UNAVEM ends its mandate and completes its withdrawal over several months, it is expected to be succeeded by a smaller U.N. observer mission that would remain until the end of the year.
